title: Club Membership: how the final early-termination fee amount is finalized
content:
## Scope
This document states, for Club Membership, how the pro-rata early-termination fee amount and its capped employer-funded offset combine into the final billed early-termination fee amount.

## Rule
The final early-termination fee amount is the pro-rata amount, less the capped employer-funded offset, rounded to 2 decimal places only at the end of the calculation, with no intermediate rounding. The final amount is never allowed to exceed the tier's own original listed early-termination fee amount, and is never billed as a negative figure.

## Worked example (hypothetical)
Suppose the pro-rata amount is $99.33, and the capped employer-funded offset, once computed, comes to $20.00. The final early-termination fee amount is $99.33 less $20.00, giving $79.33, which does not exceed the tier's own original listed early-termination fee amount.

## Points of judgement
Where no employer-funded offset applies at all, the final early-termination fee amount is simply the pro-rata amount, rounded to 2 decimal places, which by construction never exceeds the tier's own original listed early-termination fee amount; where the capped offset happens to equal the entire pro-rata amount, the final early-termination fee amount is $0.00, never a negative figure.
